admission.authority: direct user continuation of the main-backed BRC multiplier transport and priority program through exact mod-8 sparse transport
admission.reason: Extend retained root/remainder transport from consecutive/direct-from-one jumps to exact arbitrary source-target multiplier transport, enabling a nonmonotone structural priority path to reuse each already-materialized BRC state.

methods.name: BRC pairwise multiplier root/remainder transport
capabilities: exact integer root/remainder transport between arbitrary source and target multipliers <=100
one-sided lower predictor with exact odd-basin correction
safe correction bound ceil(sqrt(t/m))+1, hence <=11 globally and <=2 for downward jumps
exact nonmonotone structural-priority state stream with one initial N-dependent root
cached source-target dyadic scale constants with no new checked-in predictor payload
explicit negative audit for simple N-modular/root/remainder/phase adaptive routing shadows
methods.core_law: Given mN=J^2+R and beta=sqrt(t/m), A=floor(2^B beta), q=floor(AJ/2^B) is a lower target-root candidate with sqrt(tN)-q < beta+3/2. Therefore at most ceil(beta)+1 BRC odd-width crossings recover floor(sqrt(tN)); G=tN-q^2 is computed exactly as R+(t-m)N-(q-J)(2J+q-J), valid for both upward and downward multiplier moves.
methods.hard_boundary: Finite exact multiplier<=100 reference surface. Pairwise scale constants are cached runtime data. The simple N-dependent shadow features tested in the accompanying note are finite negative evidence only, not an independence theorem. Difference-of-squares/multiplier-Fermat/Lehman mathematics remains classical; no optimal multiplier order, asymptotic factorization speedup, or Foundation promotion is claimed.
